title: Mitigate autoscaler/cordon interaction token leak causing mixed-load queue starvation and long-context tail spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several high-severity customer escalations reported sudden p95/p99 latency regressions for short interactive requests concurrently with long-context generation workloads. The failure mode is reproducible in Dedicated and Private clusters during scale-down/cordon events and under heavy mixed-length traffic. Investigation points to an admission token accounting leak triggered by node cordon/scale-down + preemption handshake: long-context requests hold KV prefetch reservations but an edge-case in the cordon path drops their admission tokens without returning capacity to the admission reservoir, which causes the continuous batcher to block short-request flows until tokens are replenished by slow-generation completions. This manifests as queue starvation for short flows and amplified long-context tail latency across nodes.
repro_steps: Deploy mixed-length workload: 70% short chat (<=40 tokens) 30% long context (>=3k tokens) against a Dedicated pool with autoscaler enabled
Trigger a scale-down by temporarily reducing load then reintroducing a sudden microburst from short flows
Simulate node cordon using cluster control-plane (kubectl cordon/drain on one or more GPUs) while long-context requests are in-flight
Observe admission reservoir counters, continuous-batcher queue depth, and KV cache eviction rates via /metrics on the runtime nodes
Expected: short request latency stays stable. Observed: admission token deficit and starvation of short queues; p95/p99 spikes persist until long-context requests finish or node drains complete
logs_and_observations: Runtime admission_count decreased but active_batches did not shrink proportionally during cordon events
Trace span shows prefetch handshake completed, but admission_release path early-exited when cordon handler set node_state=Draining
KV cache churn increased 3x during the event causing extra memory pressure and slower generation iterations
Affected tenants span Hosted, Dedicated and Private; Dedicated clusters with aggressive autoscaler policies and low admission_safety_margin were most sensitive
Customer bug reports: two Dedicated customers and one Private on-prem customer reported 10–30s interactive stalls and subsequent error retries
root_cause_summary: A race in the node cordon/scale-down path that cancels or rehomes active generation tasks without correctly returning their admission tokens to the scheduler reservoir. The continuous batcher interprets the token deficit as full backlog and defers admission of short flows; long-context tasks hold KV/prefetch resources longer, amplifying tail latency. The autoscaler exacerbates the situation by cordoning multiple nodes in a short window, increasing the probability of token leakage across hosts.
mitigation_and_hotfixes: Hotfix 1 (canary): Reworked cordon handler to synchronously release admission tokens before transitioning tasks to draining state (cherry-pick PR runtime#9876). Canary rolled to 2 small Dedicated pools on 2026-02-11.
Hotfix 2: Add admission reservoir health check to prevent scale-down if effective_available_tokens < safety_margin (configurable by pool). Deployed as runtime feature-flag 'reservoir-protect'.
Operational mitigation: Temporary autoscaler policy change to increase min_nodes and set scale_down_delay to 120s for affected customers
Customer-specific workaround: Route latency-sensitive short flows to a dedicated low-latency pool while we complete full rollout
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Canary): runtime-1.21-hotfix canary to two low-traffic Dedicated pools and one hosted region for 48h with elevated telemetry
Stage 2 (Expanded Canary): If canary stable, deploy to 30% of Dedicated capacity and one Private customer cluster as opt-in for 72h
Stage 3 (Global): Gradual ramp to 100% across Hosted, Dedicated and Private over 1 week with feature-flag gated reservoir-protect enabled by default
Pre-rollout gating: No regression in short-request p95 and admission_token delta <= 2% from baseline for 48h
Rollback criteria: increase in short-request p95/p99 > 20% or KV eviction rate spike > 2x sustained for 15m
follow_up_tasks: Add unit and integration tests for cordon->admission token lifecycle (ENG-112234)
Design: formalize admission reservoir SLAs and expose tenant-level safety_margin controls (PM-410)
Long term: explore preemptive lightweight eviction for very long requests to cap tail latency (research spike Q2)
Improve runbook: add checklist for autoscaler tuning and emergency pool-split for affected customers
Postmortem doc and customer communication: draft postmortem and targeted mitigation steps for impacted customers
